'''''Geometry and the Imagination''''' is the  English translation of the 1932 book {{lang|de|Anschauliche Geometrie}} by [[David Hilbert]] and [[Stefan Cohn-Vossen]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Geometry and the imagination|last1=Hilbert|first1=David|author-link1=David Hilbert|last2=Cohn-Vossen|first2=Stefan|author-link2=Stefan Cohn-Vossen|date=1999|publisher=AMS Chelsea Pub|isbn=9780821819982|edition=2nd|location=Providence, R.I.|oclc=41256151}}</ref>

The book was based on a series of lectures Hilbert made in the winter of 1920–21.  The book is an attempt to present some then-current mathematical thought to "contribute to a more just appreciation of mathematics by a wider range of people than just the specialists."<ref>Hilbert, page iv</ref>  It differentiates between two tendencies in mathematics and any other scientific research: on the one hand, toward abstraction and logical relations, correlating the subject matter in a systematic and orderly manner, and on the other hand an intuitive approach, which moves toward a more immediate grasp of and a "live rapport" with the same material.  Further he asserts that intuitive understanding actually plays a major role for the researcher as well as anyone who wishes to study and appreciate Geometry.<ref>Hilbert, page iii</ref>

== Contents ==
Topics covered by the chapters in the book include the [[Leibniz formula for π|Leibniz formula for {{pi}}]], [[Configuration (geometry)|configurations of points and lines]] with equally many points on each line and equally many lines through each point,
[[curvature]] and [[non-Euclidean geometry]], [[Linkage (mechanical)|mechanical linkages]], the classification of [[manifold]]s by their [[Euler characteristic]], and the [[four color theorem]].<ref name=maa/>

== Response ==
The [[Mathematical Association of America]] said about the book, "this book is a masterpiece — a delightful classic that should never go out of print".<ref name=maa>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/geometry-and-the-imagination|title=Geometry and the Imagination {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2017-10-01}}</ref> [[Physics Today]] called it "a readable exposition of modern geometry and its relation to other branches of mathematics".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hilbert|first=D.|last2=Cohn‐Vossen|first2=S.|date=May 1953|title=Geometry and the Imagination|url=http://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.3061234|journal=Physics Today|language=en|doi=10.1063/1.3061234|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[The Scientific Monthly]] said about it "has been a classic for twenty years . . . Although it deals with elementary topics, it reaches the fringe of our knowledge in many directions".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Coxeter|first=H.S.M.|author-link=H. S. M. Coxeter|date=February 1953|title=Review: Intuitive Geometry|jstor=20643|journal=The Scientific Monthly|volume=76| issue =  2|pages=117–118}}</ref>
